strategy.summary: Reproduce the crystalball.sf precision bug by checking out the buggy commit ed184ffc1994, applying the developer's test diff, and running TestCrystalBall::test_sf. On the buggy revision sf falls back to the generic 1 - cdf, which rounds to 0 in the right tail, so the x=12.0 case (reference 1.340451684048897e-33 at rtol=1e-13) fails. On the fixed revision the _sf override uses _norm_sf for x > -beta and the same case passes. The test is compiled-extension-dependent, so a full SciPy build is required.

pinned_because: NumPy: documented only as 'SciPy is built to work with NumPy arrays'; no version constraint and no era ceiling, so the current NumPy release is chosen and this is an assumption, not evidence
Build-tool and compiler packages are general SciPy build requirements not stated in the evidence; included as era-inferred assumptions
Python version not stated in evidence; left null, use a version supported by the chosen NumPy

strategy.reproducing_test: TestCrystalBall::test_sf, parametrized over (x, beta, m, rootref) with rootref from ROOT crystalball_cdf_c, asserted with assert_allclose(sf, rootref, rtol=1e-13). The case (12.0, 1.0, 2.0, 1.340451684048897e-33) is the one that isolates the right-tail defect.
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy ed184ffc1994 with the test diff applied, test_sf fails for the right-tail cases (x=12.0, 9.0, 20) because the generic 1 - cdf path returns 0 or a value far outside rtol=1e-13 of the ROOT reference. On the fixed revision, all test_sf parametrizations pass at rtol=1e-13 against the ROOT references.
risks: Only the transition matters, and the buggy revision must be the pre-PR state; the test diff must be applied on top of it because the test is added by the PR.
The pre-fix numeric discrepancy is not stated in the evidence. The failure is predicted from the 1 - cdf mechanism and the reference value, not from a recorded buggy output.
The x threshold where precision is lost is not stated beyond 'large x'; the right-tail parametrizations (x=9, 12, 20) are chosen as the likely separators.
Under other platforms or BLAS builds the buggy 1 - cdf result may be tiny but nonzero and still fail; the transition should be confirmed, not assumed, on the target platform.
The PDF and CDF tests in the same diff tighten tolerances (rtol 1e-14 and 1e-13) and may also fail on the buggy revision, so the selection should use the test_sf node id to isolate the sf transition.
The stated 'discussion said SF looked fine' note is not evidence for the fix; the transition test is the only check used here.
If the build fails for lack of gfortran or a compatible compiler, the transition cannot be observed on this environment.

oracle.reference_source: ROOT ::Math::crystalball_cdf_c, as recorded in the PR test comments
oracle.why: The test compares the survival function against high-precision ROOT values, so a 1e-13 relative bound separates the accurate _norm_sf path from the inaccurate 1 - cdf path.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Buggy sf uses generic 1 - cdf; for x=12.0, beta=1.0, m=2.0 the cdf rounds to 1.0, so sf returns 0.0 and assert_allclose(0.0, 1.340451684048897e-33, rtol=1e-13) fails. The same mechanism applies to x=9.0 and x=20 cases.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: Fixed _sf returns the Gaussian-branch value _norm_pdf_C*_norm_sf(x)/M for x > -beta and the power-law tail otherwise, so all test_sf cases agree with ROOT references within rtol=1e-13.
